en.0: Hello, my Harry Potter Challenge family.
en.2: Thanks for joining me again today.
en.3: Last time, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall had just met, right?
en.5: This is the part where their conversation keeps going.
en.6: The thing I really want to point out today is where their personalities show through.
en.8: When McGonagall speaks, it's impatiently, coldly, testily…
en.9: Words like that keep coming up.
en.10: You can just picture her strict personality, right?
en.13: No matter what happens, this man doesn't waver.
en.14: Not a single word changes, and yet their personalities come alive, don't they?
en.15: There's a spot where McGonagall snaps at him, half exasperated.
en.16: The word exasperated shows up there, and pronouncing that final -ed sound all the way through matters more than you'd think.
en.17: If you let it trail off, it sounds like the feeling isn't finished yet.
en.19: McGonagall glances sideways at Dumbledore, and here it uses glance.
en.20: Her head stays put, only her eyes flick to the side.
en.21: If you stare intently, that's stare, and if you snap your head around, that's jerk.
en.22: 'To look' comes in all these different forms.
en.23: And McGonagall says you mustn't lose your cool — funny thing is, in Korean we say excitement moves your chest.
en.24: But here they say you 'lose your head.'
en.25: They see reason as living in the head.
en.26: A little strange, but kind of fun, right?
en.28: McGonagall flatters him, saying he's the only one Voldemort ever feared, and Dumbledore fires back playfully.
en.30: I haven't blushed so much since Madam Pomfrey told me she liked my new earmuffs." He says it's lucky it's dark, so you can't see him blush.
en.31: The word used for gently deflecting a compliment like this is flatter.
en.32: It means to make something sound better than it is — in Korean, we'd say 'putting someone on a plane.'
en.33: The world's greatest wizard joking around like this when he's complimented — kind of cute, isn't it?
en.34: Then the conversation suddenly turns heavy.
en.35: The news that the Potters were killed by Voldemort.
en.37: But what's even more shocking — baby Harry survived.
en.39: That's when they use the word astounding.
en.40: McGonagall asks how in the world Harry survived, and there's an expression here that really emphasizes 'in the world.'
en.41: It has that same feeling as our 'my goodness, how could this happen.'
en.42: Now, here Dumbledore pulls out a strange watch.
en.43: It has twelve hands but no numbers at all.
en.44: What could this watch be pointing to?
en.47: Some of you have been reading for three years, some of you are here for the first time, some of you stopped and came back — you're all here.
en.50: This was Stella, and I'll see you again tomorrow.
